# Solar watts to recharge a 1,000 Wh power station

**About 200 W of panels refills it in roughly 1.5 days. About 300-340 W refills it in one good sunny day.**

## The formula
Panel watts ≈ 1,000 Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The 0.7-0.75 factor covers heat, panel angle, and charge-controller losses ([Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts for a full recharge in one day |
|---|---|
| 3 (winter or cloudy) | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 | ~270 W |
| 6 (summer or Southwest) | ~230 W |

Source: [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/). Another guide puts a full-day summer recharge at about 300 W and a northern winter one at 700 W or more ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

## Rule of thumb
- A 200 W panel on an average day (4.5 peak sun hours, 70% efficiency) puts in about 630 Wh. That refills 1,000 Wh in a little over a day and a half ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- A 400 W array does it in under a day, about 1,260 Wh/day ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).

## Check before you buy
- **Solar input limit:** Your station caps how many watts it accepts. Panels beyond the cap add nothing on a clear day, though modest oversizing helps in weak light ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)).
- **Voltage window:** Make sure the panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) stays within the station's input range. Exceeding it can damage the charge controller. Wiring panels in series adds voltage, so be careful there ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Using power while charging:** If you run devices during the day, net charging is slower, since it's solar input minus load ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

## One option if you want 400 W
The [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel) lists at $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26 (the listing says it expires 2026-12-30). It has a 45.3 V Voc and suits 12-60 V solar inputs, and its MC4 connector comes with XT60 and DC adapters. It weighs 18.5 kg, which is heavy for a folding panel, and it's too high-voltage for stations with low input limits, such as 5-24 V or 12-28 V units.
